title: Hunza Express
summary: Six days from Lahore to Hunza over Babusar Top: Karimabad, its forts, Attabad Lake and the Passu Cones, with three nights in the valley.

image.alt: The Hunza valley from Eagle’s Nest, the river winding between villages and poplars under snow peaks

overview.headline: Three nights in Hunza, over Babusar Top and back in six days
paragraphs: The shortest way to see Hunza properly. We break the drive in Naran, cross Babusar Top in the morning light and reach Karimabad by evening, with three nights there to settle in.
In Hunza you see the forts at Baltit and Altit, take a boat on Attabad Lake and drive up to the Passu Cones, then come home the same way.
suitedTo: Families and couples with a week off who want Hunza without rushing
Travellers who want summer weather; the pass is open June to September
Anyone who prefers one base for most of the trip
notSuitedTo: Travellers who want Skardu too (see the Hunza & Skardu Grand)
Anyone who dislikes long road days: days 2 and 5 are over 10 hours
Dates outside summer, when Babusar Top is closed

faqs.question: Is Babusar Top open on our dates?
faqs.answer: The pass usually opens in June and closes by late September, which is why this trip runs only in summer. If snow closes it early, we take the longer Karakoram Highway route through Besham and tell you the new timings on WhatsApp.

faqs.question: Will the altitude affect me?
faqs.answer: Karimabad is about 2,400 m and Babusar Top over 4,000 m, where we stop only for photos and tea. Most travellers feel fine; drink water and take it slowly.

faqs.question: What are the roads like? What if the weather delays us?
faqs.answer: The Karakoram Highway is paved but mountainous, and landslides can close sections, especially in spring. Your driver adjusts the plan and we keep you updated on WhatsApp. If a closure adds a night, we arrange the hotel and agree the cost with you before you decide.
